brief.title: Midterm brief: Monday, October 12
brief.markdown:
# Midterm brief: Monday, October 12

## Bottom line
Forecasters rate the House as leaning Democratic: 9 of 10 House forecasters have more seats rated for Democrats than for Republicans, and Inside Elections is the exception at 209 D / 210 R ([Wikipedia ratings table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_election_ratings)). The Senate is closer: 46 D and 45 R seats are solid or likely, with 9 competitive ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). Markets price Democratic control at 90.5% for the House ([Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026)) and 63.5% for the Senate ([Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-senate-in-2026)), as of Oct 12. All of these are unchanged from yesterday.

## What moved
- **Louisiana Senate:** Silver Bulletin moved its rating from Likely R to Solid R, as of Oct 9 ([Wikipedia ratings table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). The race was already outside the competitive band, so the consensus doesn't change. Nothing else crossed a threshold.

## Races to watch today
- **Kansas Senate (Tossup):** KMBC reports a new poll with Marshall and Hamilton less than a point apart ([KMBC via Google News](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinwFBVV95cUxQWHpwaDJ3bGdQMmllLVl4QVZKNXI3c1pDaWlvQ3ZKZkQ3V09oU1QzclVUT25XNE9xYm1COUFzRlY1SVlNVFZzSXBOaUUydHV4d0tUaTN5WWRlRDkwZGx0OTFWNzIzOUZxeGRtRFliRS1XTU42M0xvSWRHLUx0NXdfM1dHSC13cFlJWUFWaGhDRENEd1h0ellJeGxkazByLVU?oc=5)). The poll isn't in the tracker's average yet; the two-poll average is D+2.0.
- **Maine Senate (Tossup):** The NYT reports anxious Democrats bringing in Bernie Sanders to energize Troy Jackson's campaign ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/11/us/politics/maine-bernie-sanders-troy-jackson-seante-democrats.html)). The latest poll, Washington Post/Schar School, shows Jackson 50, Collins 45, ending Oct 5 ([WaPo](https://www.washingtonpost.com/tablet/2026/10/09/sept-30-oct-5-2026-washington-post-schar-school-poll-maine-voters)).
- **Iowa Senate (Tossup):** Emerson/Nexstar shows Hinson 46.6, Turek 45.0, ending Oct 6 ([Emerson](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1mKToIlrAwY0ehEA60PVFemP5WjwxsTxN/edit?rtpof=true&sd=true)); average D+0.5.
- **Ohio Senate special (Tossup):** co/efficient, a Republican-aligned pollster, shows Husted 46, Brown 45, ending Oct 6 ([co/efficient](https://battlegrounds.coefficient.org/oh)); average D+2.5.
- **Texas Senate (Tossup):** Beacon/Shaw for Fox News shows Talarico 51, Paxton 49, ending Sep 28 ([Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/fox-news-poll-its-lone-star-senate-showdown-between-talarico-paxton)); average D+2.2.

## What the spectrum is saying
- **Left:** Pod Save America's latest episode, with David Axelrod, centers on Democrats' closing argument ([Pod Save America](https://audioboom.com/posts/8962811)).
- **Center-left:** The NYT reports Elon Musk has put $276 million into an effort to rescue Republicans in the midterms ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/12/us/politics/elon-musk-midterms.html)). NPR reports Trump struggling to convince voters he is focused on the cost of living ([NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/12/nx-s1-5998073/trump-struggles-to-show-voters-hes-focused-on-the-cost-of-living)).
- **Center-right:** The WSJ reports a growing number of Republicans warning of a weak midterm showing ([WSJ](https://www.wsj.com/politics/elections/trump-midterm-election-strategy-e4cfea75?mod=rss_socialpoliticsfeed)).
- **Right:** The Megyn Kelly Show's Oct 12 update questions Talarico's absence from the campaign trail, which he attributed to the flu (the episode's link goes to the show's general page, not the episode: [Megyn Kelly Show](https://www.siriusxm.com)). This is opinion, not reporting.

## Talking points
- The generic ballot averages D+7.2 across 4 polls; Pew has D+8, ending Oct 4 ([Pew](https://www.pewresearch.org/politics/2026/10/08/with-americans-in-a-sour-mood-democratic-voters-are-more-engaged-in-midterms)).
- Presidential approval averages 36.5% approve / 62.0% disapprove across 2 polls; RMG has 43/56, ending Oct 6 ([RMG](https://napolitannews.org/jobapproval#10-06-2026)), and Pew has 30/68 ([Pew](https://www.pewresearch.org/politics/2026/10/08/with-americans-in-a-sour-mood-democratic-voters-are-more-engaged-in-midterms)).
- Polymarket's most likely combination is a Democratic House and Senate, at 61.5%; second is a Republican Senate with a Democratic House, at 28.5% ([Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/balance-of-power-2026-midterms)).

## Coverage note
All 24 sources reported. Kalshi had no priced markets. Candidate parties remain unresolved for FL-22, MT-01, SC-01 and TX-35, so polls in those races are excluded from averages.
